display.purpose: Home masthead wordmark only, thread woven through it and tied off in the knot; sized from the column so word plus knot (about 5.9em) always fit.

headline.purpose: Inner page titles in the page head.

headline-feature.purpose: Title beside a large book on a wine field (home lead and review page h1).

title.purpose: Side-head section names and the team-page name; compact contributor names sit just under it at 1.75rem.

title-entry.purpose: Review titles in entries, prose subheads, the running-head brand and the archive category index.

quote.purpose: The highlighted passage on the home page, opening quote hung in the margin.

standfirst.purpose: Muted paragraph under a page title, max 36rem; also credit lines, the team-page bio, the footer statement and in-prose blockquotes.

body-reading.purpose: Review and about prose, max 38rem; three-line wine drop cap opens reviews.

body.purpose: Default text; also summaries, bios and the masthead description.

label.purpose: Archivo voice for every editorial link (More, WhatsApp, Instagram) and nav item.

meta.purpose: Archivo bylines, categories, dates, reading time, facts and legends, counts, figcaptions, footer note; tabular numerals, muted.

shadows.name: shadow-book
shadows.purpose: A book resting on the page: every cover, uploaded or typeset.

shadows.name: shadow-book-raised
shadows.purpose: A book picked up: its entry is hovered or keyboard-focused.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing for hairlines, arrows, lifts and transitions.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Nav hairline, arrow nudges, unpaired cover fade.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Things that travel: book lift and the cover flying into the review page.

motion.name: nav-mark-slide
motion.purpose: Highlighter sliding to the next nav item across page navigations.

motion.name: pull-thread
motion.purpose: Masthead thread wiped across the name once on load.

motion.name: tie-knot
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0 over pathLength 1; one continuous stroke (figure-eight bow and tail), 1.1s cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.25, 1) from 1s; hidden until it starts
motion.purpose: The masthead knot tying itself after the thread is through the name; static under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All movement and shared-element naming apply only when motion is welcome; otherwise pages crossfade.

motion.name: book-turn
motion.value: translateY(--lift: -4px) rotateY(--turn: 12deg), origin left, perspective 2x book height, 450ms ease-out
motion.purpose: A listed book picked up on hover or keyboard focus; touch skips it; no movement under reduced motion (shadow only).

motion.name: reading-thread
motion.value: scaleX 0 to 1 on a view timeline of the review prose, animation-range: contain; longhands only
motion.purpose: Reading progress drawn with the logo's thread; decorative; absent without scroll-driven animation support.

motion.name: highlight-sweep
motion.value: background-size 0% to 100% on the quote's view timeline, animation-range: entry 25% cover 50%; longhands only
motion.purpose: Quoted passages marked line by line as they rise into view; static and fully marked under reduced motion or without support.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Thread-Bound Magazine"**

Entre Laços is set like an independent literary magazine, and the one ornament it allows itself is the structure that binds it: the pink thread of the logo's "laço". The thread is woven over and under the masthead wordmark and tied off in a knot after the name, it joins sections as a running stitch instead of a printer's rule, it crosses every typeset book cover as the publisher's band, and it ends tied in the same knot at the top of the wine "Expediente" footer, where pink thread on wine reproduces the logo itself. If a new surface needs a divider, a band or an ending, it uses the thread; it does not invent a second ornament.

Color behaves like the materials of a bound book. Wine is the bookcloth and owns whole fields edge to edge; the logo's pink has two related jobs, the thread that binds and the reader's highlighter that marks, and never fills; light pink is the endpaper, where the contributors live; everything else is warm paper and ink. Type is one press serif (Piazzolla, with its optical-size axis) carrying the masthead and the long reading text alike, with a grotesque (Archivo) speaking only for bylines, dates, navigation and links. Books are physical objects: the only things on the page that cast shadows, lift when picked up, and fly into the review page when opened.

Density is editorial, not dashboard: generous vertical air between sections, a side-head column beside a wider main column, one reading measure, asymmetric feature compositions where the book hangs over the bottom edge of its cloth. The site refuses the landing-page hero with a button, the card grid, pill buttons, and colored call-to-action boxes; actions read as underlined editorial links with a small drawn arrow.
keyCharacteristics: One ornament, the logo's pink thread: woven wordmark ending in its knot, running stitch, cover band, footer knot.
Wine fields as bookcloth; pink only binds (thread) or marks (highlighter), never fills; light-pink endpaper for people.
Piazzolla for everything read, Archivo for everything scanned (bylines, meta, nav, links).
Books are the only objects with depth; nothing else has a shadow or a card frame.
Editorial links with SVG arrows instead of buttons.
Motion is mechanical and meaningful (thread wipe and knot tying, cover flight, highlighter slide), always gated by `prefers-reduced-motion`.

rules.name: The Bookcloth Rule
rules.body: Wine is a field, not a box. It runs edge to edge across the viewport and carries its own text, link, meta, avatar and focus colors through the field's custom properties (`--muted`, `--avatar-bg`, `--avatar-fg`), so components never need wine variants. A page whose last section is a colored field meets the footer's wine with no strip of paper between.

rules.name: The Binds and Marks Rule
rules.body: Pink has two related jobs and no others: the thread binds (masthead thread, running stitch, cover band, knot) and the highlighter marks what the reader marks (the current nav item, quoted passages, `::selection`). It never fills a section, a panel or a cover; the light-pink endpaper is the only pink field. The highlighter's shape is a reader's stroke: low on the line (from 38% to 90% of the line box), or the nav mark cut to the book radius, never a full rectangle behind a block. The thread reads softly on paper (about 1.6:1, decorative, never text) and at full strength on wine.

rules.name: The Two Missing Tones Rule
rules.body: Typeset covers are never wine (a wine book vanishes on the wine lead field) and never pink (pink is reserved for the thread and the highlighter). New cover tones come from bookcloth, not from the brand accents.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Piazzolla is what you read; Archivo is what you scan. Titles, summaries, bios, quotes and prose are serif; bylines, dates, categories, nav, links and figcaptions are sans. No third family, and no all-caps tracked labels.

rules.name: The Credit Line Rule
rules.body: A review is always introduced with the book it reads, set as "sobre *Título*, de Autor" in the serif, muted, with the book title in italic `cite` (on wine, the cite switches to on-wine).

rules.name: The Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every text size is a ramp step above; a new element borrows the step whose role it shares (a credit line is a standfirst, a link is a label, a legend is meta) instead of minting an in-between literal.

rules.name: The One Reading Line Rule
rules.body: Main-column content on wide screens starts at the same x as the main column of the side-head grid. A new section either uses the side-head or aligns to its main column; it does not center itself.

rules.name: The Only Objects Rule
rules.body: Shadows are for books. If something that is not a book needs emphasis, it gets a field, a highlighter or the thread, never a shadow.

dos: **Do** use the thread (stitch, band, woven line, knot) as the only ornament and the only divider.
**Do** give wine whole full-bleed fields and let the field supply on-wine text, meta, avatar and focus colors.
**Do** mark with rose as a low highlighter stroke (38% to 90% of the line box) or the book-radius nav mark.
**Do** introduce every review with its book: the cover object and the "sobre *Título*, de Autor" credit line.
**Do** set reading in Piazzolla at 1.1875rem / 1.7 within 38rem, and scanned apparatus in Archivo.
**Do** keep every link and nav target at least 44px tall, with the 3px wine focus ring (on-wine or rose on wine).
**Do** gate every movement behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, keeping state changes (deeper shadow, color) without the motion.
donts: **Don't** build cards: no bordered or rounded boxes around entries, contributors or sections.
**Don't** use buttons or pill shapes for actions; use an editorial link with a drawn SVG arrow.
**Don't** fill a section, panel or cover with pink (thread or rose); the light-pink endpaper is the only pink field.
**Don't** set text in the thread color on paper; it is decorative there (about 1.6:1).
**Don't** make a typeset cover wine or pink.
**Don't** put a shadow on anything that is not a book.
**Don't** add uppercase tracked kickers or eyebrows above titles; a section is named by its serif side-head.
**Don't** add a third typeface or a printer's hairline rule between sections.
